subject: Arcturus x Redwood — integration coupling & entitlement questions
messages:
From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@arcturus.ai>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Arcturus x Redwood — integration coupling & entitlement questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Arcturus is excited about the latency/cost profile you showed. Our infra and product teams started to map out what a Redwood integration would look like for our cloud appliance offering and we've run into a few gating questions that will affect our roadmap. Quick summary below (attached: arcturus-integration-spec.pdf):

- Marketplace entitlements: we need clarity on how Redwood maps marketplace SKUs to dedicated vs hosted capacity. Can users on our subscription be automatically routed to customer-dedicated pools?
- SSO / provisioning: does Redwood support SCIM provisioning of team-level entitlements, or do we need to maintain an external mapping?
- API coupling: we plan to call Redwood's hosted API from our control plane; how stable are your model URIs and what is your recommended approach for graceful fallback to a smaller variant?
- Test staging: for our CI we require a staging entitlement that behaves like production but without billing spikes — can Redwood provide a non-billing sandbox or special test token?

We'd like to propose a short sync with your product/engineers to confirm constraints before we finalize our roadmap. Availability next week (Tue/Wed) PST — would you and the product folks be available?

Tom
Tom Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Arcturus Systems

Attachments: arcturus-integration-spec.pdf (pdf)
From: logan_wright@redwood.com <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Tom Chen <tom.chen@arcturus.ai>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arcturus x Redwood — integration coupling & entitlement questions

Tom — thanks for the clear write-up and the spec. Looping in Camila (PM), Priyom (eng), and Grace (Partner Ops) so we can answer the technical and entitlement parts. Preliminary answers below and a proposed mutual action plan attached (redwood-marketplace-checklist.xlsx):

- Marketplace entitlements: We can map marketplace SKUs to either hosted or Dedicated capacity. For automatic routing to a customer-dedicated pool we need a customer identifier at request time (tenant_id or api_key). That mapping is configurable in Dedicated; will require a short entitlement handoff during onboarding.
- SCIM provisioning: Redwood supports SCIM for user provisioning. Entitlement mapping (SKU -> capacity) is currently not provisioned via SCIM out of the box but we can accept an initial mapping via API or CSV during onboarding. Long-term we can add a SCIM extension; timeline depends on priority.
- Model URIs & fallback: We guarantee stable model version tags for 90 days; model variant fallbacks can be configured via policy (preferred_uri, fallback_uri). We'll share a suggested fallback policy during our sync.
- Staging/test tokens: We offer a test sandbox for partners on request — it mirrors production behavior but caps billable tokens and isolates logs. We can provide a test entitlement for your CI.

Proposed next steps (in the attachment): schedule 60m technical sync (Camila + Priyom), provide a sample entitlement mapping template (we'll attach), and scope a canary rollout plan. Camila, can you propose 2 time slots next Tue/Wed PST?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-07-19T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arcturus x Redwood — integration coupling & entitlement questions

Tom / Logan — thanks, and great questions. A few technical notes to inform Arcturus's architecture before the sync:

1) KV/prefix caching: If Arcturus will send long-running chat sessions from edge devices, we recommend using our session tokens + prefix caching so your control plane can attach cached KV state without re-sending full context. This reduces per-token cost and improves latency for repeated prompts.

2) Model pinning & quantization: If you intend to run in Dedicated pools with quantized weights we need to know target hardware (A100 vs H100 vs other) to recommend quantization profiles. Some older variants may not have accelerated kernels for low-latency 1-2 token responses.

3) Auth and routing headers: Include X-Redwood-Tenant and X-Redwood-Request-Intent headers to enable correct routing and QoS. We'll share a sample HTTP snippet in the shared drive.

4) Entitlement API: Priyom — can you confirm whether we can accept entitlement mapping via a REST API call during onboarding? If not, we should commit to a CSV ingest within the pilot timeline.

Tom — attaching a lightweight SOW template and our recommended API sample in the Drive link Logan included. For the meeting, we should block engineering time to walk through the KV/cache behavior and the canary rollout gating.

Camila Reyes
Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Camila / Logan — helpful — thanks. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups:

- KV/prefix caching: yes, Arcturus will adopt session token flow. We'll need a sample of the headers and best-practice TTLs.
- Hardware: our Dedicated pools will run on H100-like accelerators (cloud appliance uses H100 equivalent). Good to know about kernels — we'll plan for that.
- Entitlement API: we can accept CSVs but would prefer API-based provisioning for automation. If Redwood can expose a /v1/entitlements endpoint for our onboarding service, that's ideal.
- Staging/testing token: we would like a non-billing test entitlement with capped tokens for CI. This must not count towards our initial committed capacity.

Also — legal has flagged one item: we will need a temporary entitlement exception to boot our internal QA rigs before the marketplace listing completes. Is Redwood able to issue a time-boxed exemption or a trial license tied to our partner id? We are ready to sign an SOW; I included a DocuSign link (https://app.docusign.com/partner/ABC12345) for a standard partner SOW — please review.

Proposed meeting: Wed 2027-07-21 10:00 PST (60m). Can you confirm attendees?

Tom
